attribution.note: Zitron states and endorses the claim in his own prose.

semantics.note: The proposition fairly captures the statement when real demand means independent demand adequate to sustain the business and investment described, rather than literally no paying customers.

contract.note: The contextual reading is ordinary given the acknowledged sales and surrounding financing concerns. The quarter is a reasonable observation window. The contract appropriately avoids inventing a numerical investment-return threshold.

evidence.note: Timely company disclosure covering the target quarter. Paid seats and expansion challenge a literal absence of buyers but do not establish actual prices, durable renewals or investment adequacy.
Independent spending observations cover June. They establish purchasing activity but do not separate the software categories or connect payments to supplier costs, financing and investment returns.

Available before the cutoff and relevant to financing concerns. Its October ecosystem assessment does not establish inadequate software demand or financing dependence of customer purchases during the target quarter.

reviews.rationale: The packet documents paid adoption and financing links, but neither establishes whether representative independent demand sustains either software category over the relevant investment life. Adoption alone does not contradict the contextual claim; circular financing alone does not support it.
